title: Arrest Of Ling Foh Sung Communist Suspect On Ferry Road On 30.3.32

page_data.en:

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Special Branch S.2.
REPORT

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S. REGISTRY Special Branch S.2. SHANGHAI No. D 3435 Date MAY 17, 1932.）

Subject (in full) Result of Court Proceedings in respect Ling Foh Sung (林福生), alias Ling Ah Foh (林阿福), communist suspect, arrested on Ferry Road on March 30, 1932.
Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Ross.

With reference to your endorsement on the subject of the decision handed down in respect of a communist suspect named Ling Foh Sung (林福生) alias Ling Ah Foh (林阿福), who was arrested on a piece of vacant ground off Ferry Road on March 30, 1932, on a charge of being in possession of 16 copies of an objectionable newspaper entitled the "Young Labourers' Small Newspaper(青工小报), issue No.1," I have to report that in spite of the fact that contents of the offending publication are mainly of an anti-government and anti-Japanese nature, it may be said with certainty to be of communist origin, though it does not openly advocate communism. However, in view of the fact that the accused was detained in custody from March 30 to May 13, and that Mr. Lea, Assistant Municipal Advocate, is not prepared to appeal against the verdict, I am of the opinion that no further action be taken in the matter.

D. I.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

（批：Filed 18.5.32）

主题（全称） 关于共产主义嫌疑犯林福生（Ling Foh Sung），又名林阿福（Ling Ah Foh），于1932年3月30日在斐伦路（Ferry Road）被捕一案的法庭诉讼结果。
由 D. I. Ross 制作并呈报。

关于阁下就一名名为林福生（Ling Foh Sung）、又名林阿福（Ling Ah Foh）的共产主义嫌疑犯的判决决定所作的批示，该人于1932年3月30日因被指控持有16份名为《青工小报》第一期之违禁报刊，而在斐伦路旁的一块空地上被捕，现报告如下：尽管涉案出版物的内容主要具有反政府和反日性质，且虽未公开宣扬共产主义，但可确定其源于共产党方面。然而，鉴于被告自3月30日至5月13日被拘留，且助理市检察官 Lea 先生不准备对该判决提出上诉，本人认为此事不再采取进一步行动。

D. I.

特别支部主管警官。

（批注：归档 1932年5月18日）

EXTRACT FROM DAILY INTELLIGENCE REPORT DATED 31/3/32.

Communist Propaganda - Arrest of Communist suspect.

At 10.15 a.m. March 30, a suspected communist named Ling
Foh Sung (林福生) alias Ling Ah Foh (林阿福), was arrested on
a piece of vacant ground of Ferry Road. In his possession
was found a quantity of communist pamphlets entitled "The
Young Labourers' Small Newspaper", Issue No.1 dated March 29,
1932. This document among other matter advocates the masses to
organize armed picketing groups to attack the Municipal Police
and the Kuomintang Authorities, and requests the Chinese Soviet
Government and the Red Armies to assist the Shanghai workers in
their struggle against the Kuomintang and the Imperialists.
The arrested man will appear Before Court on March 31.
page_data.zh:
摘自1932年3月31日的每日情报报告。

共产主义宣传 - 逮捕共产主义嫌疑犯。

3月30日上午10时15分，一名名为林福生（Ling Foh Sung）、又名林阿福（Ling Ah Foh）的共产主义嫌疑人在斐伦路的一块空地上被捕。在其身上搜出大量共产主义小册子，题为《青工小报》，第一期，日期为1932年3月29日。该文件除其他内容外，鼓动群众组织武装纠察队攻击工部局警务处和国民党当局，并请求中华苏维埃政府和红军协助上海工人进行反对国民党及帝国主义的斗争。
被捕者将于3月31日出庭受审。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Ling Foh Sung, alias Ling Ah Foh.
native of Kiangse taken by me C.D.C.252.
at Pootoo Road on the 30.3.32. and interpreted by Chang Wen Ta.

My name is Ling Foh Sung, alias Ling Ah Foh, aged 19, I am a na-
tive of Kiangse, unemployed and living in the Sing Sing Zu Yee
Teashop at Thorburn Road. At 9 a.m. on the 30.3.32 I left my
home at Thorburn Road and went to Gordon Road, near Connaught
Road, where I met a Mr. Tsang, whom I asked to get me a job,
whereupon he gave me a bundle of newspapers and told me to sell
them to some workers at 3 coppers each on a vacant ground near
Robison and Ferry Roads. On arrival there I was arrested by the
Police.

Signed and cross-marked by Ling Foh Sung.

Witness: C.D.C.264.

以下是林福生，又名林阿福的供词。
江西籍，由我，刑事侦探股252号警员，
于1932年3月30日在蒲东路录取，由张文达（Chang Wen Ta）翻译。

我叫林福生，又名林阿福，19岁，江西籍，失业，居住在索伯恩路（Thorburn Road）的新新如意茶楼。1932年3月30日上午9时，我离开索伯恩路的住处，前往靠近康纳脱路（Connaught Road）的戈登路（Gordon Road），在那里遇到一位张先生，我请他帮我找份工作，随后他给了我一捆报纸，让我去罗便臣路（Robison）和斐伦路（Ferry Roads）附近的一块空地上，以每份3个铜板的价格卖给一些工人。到达那里后，我被警察逮捕。

林福生签名并画十字。

见证人：刑事侦探股264号警员。

page_data.en:
Summarized translation of a pamphlet entitled "Young
Labourers' Small Newspaper, issue No.1", dated March 29,
copies of which were found in possession of Ling Ah Poh
(林阿福) who was arrested on a piece of vacant ground
off Ferry Road on March 30, 1932. (Seized 16 copies)

Persist in the struggle against the Kuomintang
and Imperialism, and continue the strikes in
Japanese cotton mills !

The Kuomintang government has surrendered to the
Imperialists and ordered the withdrawal (? from Shanghai)
of Chinese troops, whilst the Imperialist forces including
the Shanghai Municipal Police, the plain clothes men of
the Bureau of Social Affairs, and the Foreign troops at
Shanghai are launching attacks upon the workers of
Japanese cotton mills. Let us adopt the following measures:-

1) To unite the workers of Japanese cotton mills, and
organize a general strike committee.

2) To organize picketing groups of young vanguards armed
with big swords, and wooden clubs and iron bars, for the
purpose of protecting our headquarters and attacking
detectives, plain clothes men, labour traitors, members
of the Elimination Clique, and representatives of the
Bureau of Social Affairs.

3) To include female and juvenile workers in the picketing
groups for the purpose of besieging the Government
(Municipality of Greater Shanghai) to enforce a demand
for funds and rice for the families of the unemployed.

4) To hold demonstrations of students and labourers and
collect contributions for the relief of strikers.

5) To request the Soviet Government, Red Armies, and
revolutionary soldiers and all revolutionary organizations
throughout the country to assist the Shanghai workers in
their struggle against the Kuomintang and the Imperialists.
page_data.zh:
题为《青工小报，第一期》，日期为3月29日的小册子摘要译文，该小册子在1932年3月30日于斐伦路旁一块空地上被捕的林阿福（Ling Ah Poh）（林阿福）身上搜获。（查获16份）

坚持反对国民党和帝国主义的斗争，继续日本纱厂的罢工！

国民党政府已向帝国主义投降，并命令中国军队撤出（?从上海），而包括上海公共租界工部局警务处、社会局便衣人员以及在上海的外国军队在内的帝国主义势力，正在向日本纱厂的工人发动攻击。让我们采取以下措施：-

1) 团结日本纱厂工人，组织总罢工委员会。

2) 组织由手持大刀、木棍和铁条的青年先锋队组成的武装纠察队，目的是保护我们的总部，并攻击侦探、便衣人员、工贼、清除共党派成员和社会局代表。

3) 将女工和童工纳入纠察队，目的是包围政府（大上海市政府），强制要求为失业者家属提供资金和大米。

4) 举行学生和劳工示威游行，并募集捐款以救济罢工者。

5) 请求苏维埃政府、红军、革命士兵及全国所有革命组织协助上海工人进行反对国民党及帝国主义的斗争。

Charge Poss. of Anti-Government and Communistic Literature. Cont. to Art.
2 of the Law Governing Punishment of Persons who commit acts with
intent to injure the Republic of China and Art. 106 of the CCRC.
For that he at 10.15 a.m. on the 30/3/32 on a piece of vacant
ground off Ferry road did have in his possession a number of anti
government and communistic pamphlets, for the purpose of distrib-
uting same.

Proceedings Mr. T. S. Lea appeared for the Police.
Accused :- I was selling newspapers sometime ago. I came to
Shanghai to see a friend for the purpose of finding a job, but I
could not find one, so I sold newspapers. The communists are very
active in my province (Kiangse) but not in my district. I was living
in Pootung and I went to Connaught Road to find work. I met a man
named Tsang who used to buy newspapers from me. I ask him to get me a job.
He said alright and then he gave a bundle of mosquito papers wrapped
up and he told me those were of Anti-Japanese nature, and told me to
sell them. He told me that he was working in a Japanese Press. I
was selling newspapers of all kinds at North Szechuen Road. I cannot
read well. I only studied a few old Chinese books for one year when
I was about 13 years of age. He told me to sell at a Big Clock Stand
on Ferry Road to workers at 3 coppers each. I met Tsang at a Bridge
off Connaught Road and Gordon Road. I do not know where he resides.
I did not read the paper. I was arrested by Police but I sell my
papers to any one. I did not know the papers were communist
nature until I was told by the Police. I never sold papers of this
kind and never sold any to workers. I walked from Gordon Road to
Ferry Road and it took me half an hour. I went to Ferry Road as
told by him because every newspaper seller is detailed to a certain
place to sell. This is the usual system. (Here seized papers produc-
ed by Mr. Lea). I did not ask Tsang where is the Press of the papers
I intended to find him if I could sell of the papers given by him.
Tsang said it was a daily paper. I gave him my address for him to
find me. I did not think it was a strange case when he gave me the

事由：1932年3月30日上午10时15分，其在斐伦路（Ferry road）旁的一块空地上，持有多份反政府及共产主义小册子，意图分发。

诉讼程序 李T.S.先生（Mr. T. S. Lea）代表警方出庭。
被告：— 我前段时间在卖报纸。我来上海是为了见一个朋友并找工作，但没找到，所以就卖报纸。我的省份（江西）共产党很活跃，但我所在的地区并不活跃。我住在浦东，我去康纳特路（Connaught Road）找工作。我遇到一个叫曾（Tsang）的人，他以前从我这里买报纸。我请他帮我找份工作。他说好的，然后给了我一包用报纸包着的“蚊子报”（mosquito papers，指小型或廉价报纸），并告诉我那些是抗日性质的，让我去卖。他说他在一家日本报社工作。我在北四川路卖各种报纸。我识字不多。我大约13岁时只读了一年旧式中文书。他让我在斐伦路的一个大钟亭向工人出售，每份3个铜板。我在康纳特路和戈登路（Gordon Road）交界处的一座桥边遇到了曾。我不知道他住在哪里。我没有读那些报纸。我被警察逮捕了，但我把报纸卖给任何人。直到警察告诉我，我才知道这些报纸具有共产主义性质。我从未卖过这类报纸，也从未向工人出售过任何此类报纸。我从戈登路走到斐伦路，花了半个小时。我按他的吩咐去了斐伦路，因为每个报贩都被指派到特定地点售卖。这是通常的制度。（此处出示李先生查获的报纸）。我没有问曾这些报纸是哪家报社印刷的，我想如果我能卖掉他给我的报纸，再去找他。曾说那是日报。我给了他我的地址以便他找我。当他给我

that communist were arrest on Ferry Road vicinity quite recently.
C.D.C.264 :- At 9.50 a.m. I received information that a meeting
would be held on a piece of vacant ground. I was detailed by my of-
ficer in charge. I proceeded there and I saw the accused was reading
and distributing to workers standing around him. About 20 workers
were there. We arrested the accused and seized the produced papers.
White papers were in his left hand and the printed papers were in
his right hand. When I approached, the accused became quiet.
Accused :- Tsang rolled up the papers when he gave me. 3 others
were arrested beside me and they were released. They were standing
near me and searched and found nothing.
Mr. Lea :- The police arrested 4 person including the accused
( 3 men and 1 woman). The others gave proper address and enquiries
proved that there was not sufficient evidence to charge them so they
were released. The accused gave his address as 116 Thorburn Road
and the police made enquiries. The inmates of 116 Thorburn Road
told Police they did not know the accused.
Accused :- I removed to 116 Thorburn Road 2 days after the war
broke out in Shanghai. I had $13.00 there. I have never sold newspap-
ers since the war in Shanghai. The inmates refused to recognize me
because I was handcuffed then and the police told them I was a com-
munist. Only 2 men and 1 woman were standing near me. I could not
accept the papers and proceed to Ferry Road if I knew this is com-
munist propaganda.
Judge to accused :- I will remand the case.
Decision Remand sine die.
Accused to be detained in custody.

报纸时，我并不觉得奇怪，但现在我觉得奇怪了。我不看日报，所以我不知道最近斐伦路附近有人因共产主义活动被捕。
刑事侦缉处警员264号：— 上午9时50分，我收到情报称将有一场集会在某块空地上举行。我的主管警官指派我前往。我到达那里，看到被告正在阅读并向围在他周围的工人分发材料。现场约有20名工人。我们逮捕了被告并缴获了出示的报纸。白纸在他左手，印刷品在他右手。当我走近时，被告变得安静下来。
被告：— 曾给我报纸时把它们卷起来了。除了我之外还有3人被捕，他们后来被释放了。他们站在我附近，经过搜身未发现任何东西。
李先生：— 警察逮捕了包括被告在内的4人（3男1女）。其他人提供了确切地址，经调查证明证据不足以致控，因此被释放。被告提供的地址是韬伯恩路（Thorburn Road）116号，警方进行了查询。韬伯恩路116号的住户告诉警方他们不认识被告。
被告：— 上海战事爆发两天后，我搬到了韬伯恩路116号。我在那里有13美元。自上海战事以来，我从未卖过报纸。住户拒绝承认认识我，因为我当时戴着手铐，而且警察告诉他们我是共产党。只有2名男子和1名妇女站在我附近。如果我知道这是共产主义宣传，我就不会接受这些报纸并前往斐伦路。
法官对被告说：— 我将还押本案。
裁决 无限期还押候审。
被告予以羁押。

编号
$2 / 待处理

Proceedings.
Mr T.S.Lee appeared for the Police.
Mr Loh Ting Ming appeared for the accused.

Accused in reply to Judge :- I was a newspaper vendor before,
but I am now unemployed.

Mr Lee :- On the 30th March at 10.15.a.m, the Police received
information that labourers were going to hold a meeting on Ferry Road
near Robison Road, so the police proceeded there and saw the accused
with 3 other suspects, and at the time the accused was distributing
pamphlets, so they were all taken to the station, and the 3 suspects
were released on account of lack of evidence. When the accused was
questioned, he stated he lived at 116 Thorburn Road, so the police
made enquiries and found this to be untrue. He then said a man named
Tsang gave him the pamphlets, and further stated he did not know the
contents of them and the papers.

Accused :- I was arrested at about 10.a.m on the 30th March
on Ferry Road in possession of a parcel of papers, the contents of
which I did not know. I was going to sell them, as I thought they
were mosquito papers. On that morning, I met a man named Tsang on
Gordon Road, and he gave me the papers to sell. I asked him what was
the contents of them and he said they were of an Anti-Japanese nature.
I went to the piece of ground on Ferry Road near Robison Road with
a view of selling these papers. I did live in the house on Taku Road
where I took the police, but the inmates were afraid to tell the
police so. I did not distribute any papers, and I have never sold
any papers like them before, neither can I read Chinese very well.
My friend named Tsang was formerly employed in the Japanese Press.
I sold various kinds of papers before when I was a news-vendor.

Counsel summed up.

Decision. Pleading closed. Remand for judgment till 13.5.32, at 1.30.p.m
F.BOURNE.

(批：Noted Kwh 11/5)
(批：Sg. Further report in due course. D. Kirk. See and pass a Reg. J.R. 11/5:32.)

诉讼程序。
李T.S.先生代表警方出庭。
罗廷明先生（Mr Loh Ting Ming）代表被告出庭。

被告回答法官：— 我以前是报贩，但现在失业了。

李先生：— 3月30日上午10时15分，警方收到情报称劳工将在斐伦路靠近罗宾森路（Robison Road）的地方举行集会，于是警方前往该处，看到被告与其他3名嫌疑人在一起，当时被告正在分发小册子，因此他们全部被带到警局，另外3名嫌疑人因证据不足被释放。审讯被告时，他声称住在韬伯恩路116号，警方经查询发现此言不实。随后他说是一个叫曾的人给了他这些小册子，并进一步声称他不知道这些小册子和报纸的内容。

被告：— 3月30日上午10点左右，我在斐伦路因持有一包报纸而被捕，我不知道其中的内容。我打算去卖它们，因为我以为它们是“蚊子报”。那天早上，我在戈登路遇到一个叫曾的人，他给我报纸去卖。我问它们的内容是什么，他说具有抗日性质。我带着这些报纸前往斐伦路靠近罗宾森路的那块空地，打算出售。我确实住在带警察去的大沽路（Taku Road）的那所房子里，但住户害怕不敢这样告诉警察。我没有分发任何报纸，以前也从未卖过像这样的报纸，而且我的中文阅读能力很差。我的朋友曾以前在日本报社工作。我以前做报贩时卖过各种报纸。

律师总结陈词。

裁决。 答辩结束。还押以待判决，时间为1932年5月13日下午1时30分
F. BOURNE。

（批注：已知悉 Kwh 5月11日）
